lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is the Telluride Regional Medical Center board meeting Wednesday, where the board goes into executive session and then takes public action on interim hospital leadership — that's consequential for everyone in this valley who depends on that facility. Alongside that, Mountain Village takes up an ordinance that would move housing authority fees out of municipal code into an annually updated fee schedule, San Miguel County's housing code working group holds its eighth session on stripping out Land Use Code barriers to workforce housing, and HARC gets a work session on a potential demolition and rebuild of Rebekah Hall — the building where they meet.

notable.stake: County working group targets Land Use Code barriers to affordable housing production.
HARC considers potential demolition and rebuild of historic Town-owned Rebekah Hall.
BOCC takes up Constitutional Amendments and a view-plain MOU with real land-use teeth.
Two public hearings — Curry PUD and a parcel subdivision — open for public comment.
First reading: ordinance shifting housing authority fees out of Mountain Village municipal code.
P&Z reviews Comp Plan update shaping long-range land use and density for all of Telluride.
Board votes in public on who leads the regional medical center in the near term.
